evidence.claim: asyncio.gather propagates an unhandled exception to the caller immediately
evidence.quote: By default, if a coroutine is executed by asyncio.gather() fails with an unhandled exception, it will be propagated to the caller.
evidence.title: Asyncio gather() Handle Exceptions

evidence.claim: asyncio.gather does not automatically cancel remaining coroutines when one fails
evidence.quote: For asyncio.gather(...) with default arguments (return_exceptions=False), this means the first encountered exception is immediately re‑raised to the awaiting code, and gathering stops there.
evidence.title: asyncio.gather Exceptions: Check Which Tasks Still Run
sub_questions: Does asyncio.gather cancel the remaining coroutines when one fails?

evidence.claim: To cancel all tasks when one fails, you must manually cancel them or cancel the gather future
evidence.quote: You can cancel all tasks when one task fails when using asyncio.gather() by manually traversing the list of tasks can cancel them manually.

evidence.claim: Setting return_exceptions=True causes asyncio.gather to trap unhandled exceptions and return them as results instead of propagating them.
evidence.quote: Setting the 'return_exceptions' argument to True will trap any unhandled exceptions and provide them as return values, allowing all other tasks in the group to complete.
